s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic, violaceous, annular skin lesions localized to one axilla
salient_findings: Discrete, dark red, circular lesions in the right axilla
Severe pruritus at the lesion sites
Well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion
key_facts: Male patient in his 40s
3-month history of skin lesions
Lesions are limited to the right axilla
Severe pruritus wakes the patient up at night
No recent trauma or history of similar lesions
No associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms
Unremarkable medical history
No environmental triggers or new medications
No improvement with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, or discontinuation of underarm deodorant
Negative Wood lamp examination
Biopsy shows lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction

per_call: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands

shortlist.label: Lichen planus pigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of violaceous, annular patches and severe pruritus

shortlist.label: Inverse lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the location and appearance of the lesions

shortlist.label: Lichenoid drug eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the lack of response to treatments and presence of pruritus

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of annular lesions and severe pruritus

shortlist.label: Granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: Annular lesions and lack of systemic symptoms make it a plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches limited to the right axilla, along with severe pruritus and biopsy findings showing lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction, is most consistent with inverse lichen planus, which typically affects intertriginous areas such as the axilla.

rejected.label: Lichen planus pigmentosus
rejected.why: Lichen planus pigmentosus typically presents with diffuse hyperpigmentation rather than discrete, annular patches.

rejected.label: Lichenoid drug eruption
rejected.why: There is no reported history of new medications that could trigger a lichenoid drug eruption.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Discoid lupus erythematosus typically presents with scaly, erythematous plaques, which are not described in this case.

rejected.label: Granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Granuloma annulare typically presents with papular lesions that form an annular pattern, but the biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis.
